answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a bonded violet registry: each agent locks a refundable stake before its work counts, and peers countersign every task before payout. Forging a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand stakes, so attack costs scale linearly while honest agents recover their bond plus fees. Reputation grows only through verified jobs, so new identities carry no weight, and proven fraud triggers slashing that burns the bond. A wharf ledger records earned standing, and a horizon audit rechecks attestations, so fraud costs more than it pays.
